gaps.hint: an unspecified day in the future
gaps.explanation: 'Another day' means some other, unspecified day; 'the other day' refers to the recent past.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ of the villagers had ever seen a passport.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly any of' = almost none of; 'hardly none' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so 'how much' is used.

gaps.sentence: She's very fussy — she refuses to eat ___ green.
gaps.hint: after 'refuse' the clause is negative in meaning
gaps.explanation: Verbs like refuse, deny and avoid create a negative context, so 'anything' is used.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with excuses; deliver on time or do not bother coming.
gaps.explanation: 'Has no patience with' — 'no' directly negates the noun.
